Today, the Hmong in China are categorized under the umbrella term Miáo (苗) along with three other indigenous cultural groups, which include non-Hmong peoples such as the Hmu and the Xong of southeast Guizhou. What is Hmong music? From ancestral echoes to modern melodies, the story of Hmong music is a symphony of resilience, joy, and cultural pride. Hmong music is a kaleidoscope of sounds that intertwine to create a harmonious blend of tradition and cultural identity. Why are instruments important in Hmong music? Instruments are an important part of Hmong music because of the Hmong Whistled Language, a more advance language in which language is communicated through the manipulation of the tongue, shape of the mouth, and tones to create an effect of the Hmong Language. Why do some Hmong people call themselves Miao? Scholarly and commercial exchanges, increasingly made over the internet, have also resulted in an exchange of terminology, including some Hmong people accepting the designation Miao after visiting China and some nationalist non-Hmong Miao peoples identifying as Hmong. Is Hmong a singular or plural name? The term Hmong is the English spelling of the Hmong's native name. It is a singular and plural noun (e.g., Japanese, French, etc.). Very little is known about the native Hmong name as it is not mentioned in Chinese historical records, since the Han identified the Hmong as Miao.
